issues.title: Test file separated from hook
issues.description: The rule requires test files to be co-located with their corresponding component files in the same directory. The test file use-state-favicon.test.ts was moved to ui-v2/src/__tests__/hooks/ instead of remaining in ui-v2/src/hooks/ with the hook file use-state-favicon.ts.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: Incorrect falsy value handling for run_count displays wrong value for zero
issues.description: The run_count display uses the logical OR operator (||) instead of the nullish coalescing operator (??). This causes a bug when run_count is explicitly 0 (a valid value indicating the task has not been retried). When run_count is 0, the || operator treats it as falsy and displays the fallback value '0' instead of the actual value 0 from the API. While the visual output is the same, this semantic error means the code doesn't distinguish between 'no data' (null/undefined) and 'zero retries' (0), which could cause issues if the UI behavior needs to differentiate these states in the future or if the fallback value changes.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
<dl className="flex flex-col gap-1 mb-2">
	<dt className="text-gray-500">Run Count</dt>
	<dd className="">{taskRun.run_count || 0}</dd>
</dl>

issues.title: Missing type coercion for retries value causes potential type inconsistency
issues.description: The retries display removes the .toString() call that was present in the original PR, directly rendering taskRun.empirical_policy?.retries ?? "0". This creates a type inconsistency where the value could be either a number (when retries exists) or a string "0" (when it doesn't). While React can render both, this inconsistency violates the principle of uniform data handling and could cause issues in the component tree if parent or child components expect consistent string formatting for this field, or if the value is later used in string operations or comparisons.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
<dl className="flex flex-col gap-1 mb-2">
	<dt className="text-gray-500">Retries</dt>
	<dd className="">
		{taskRun.empirical_policy?.retries ?? "0"}
	</dd>
</dl>

issues.title: Incorrect truthy check for retry_jitter_factor hides valid zero values
issues.description: The retry_jitter_factor check was changed from an explicit null/undefined check to a simple truthy check. This is a critical bug because a jitter factor of 0 is a valid configuration value (meaning no randomness in retry delays), but the truthy check treats 0 as falsy and displays "None" instead. This misrepresents the actual task configuration to users, making them think no jitter factor is set when it's actually configured to 0. The original PR correctly distinguished between 'not set' (null/undefined) and 'set to zero' (0), but this change breaks that distinction.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
<dl className="flex flex-col gap-1 mb-2">
	<dt className="text-gray-500">Retry Jitter Factor</dt>
	<dd className="">
		{taskRun.empirical_policy?.retry_jitter_factor
			? taskRun.empirical_policy.retry_jitter_factor.toString()
			: "None"}
	</dd>
</dl>

issues.title: Missing test file for new use-state-favicon hook violates repository testing rules
issues.description: A new hook use-state-favicon.ts was added without a corresponding test file. This directly violates AGENTS.md Rule #10 requiring test files to be co-located with their components/hooks, and ui-v2/src/hooks/AGENTS.md which states 'Code, test, and related files should be in the same directory'. The ui-v2/AGENTS.md also explicitly requires 'Always write tests for new components and hooks' as a quality standard. All other hooks in the directory have test files (use-page-title.test.ts, use-stepper.test.ts, etc.), making this omission a clear violation of established patterns and explicit repository rules.

issues.title: Flow run link displays empty or undefined text when flow_run_name is missing
issues.description: The condition for displaying the flow run link was changed from checking both flow_run_id AND flow_run_name to only checking flow_run_id. When a task run has a flow_run_id but flow_run_name is null or undefined (which is valid according to the UITaskRun schema where flow_run_name is 'string | null | undefined'), the link will render with empty text or display 'undefined'. This creates a broken user experience where users see a clickable link with no visible text. The original code correctly ensured both values existed before showing the link.

	<dl className="flex flex-col gap-1 mb-2">

		<dd>

				to="/runs/flow-run/$id"

				className="text-blue-500 hover:underline cursor-pointer flex items-center"
			>
				<Icon id="ExternalLink" className="mr-1 size-4" />
				{taskRun.flow_run_name}
			</Link>
		</dd>
	</dl>

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #19951 - feat(ui-v2): improve task run details page parity with Vue

structured_output.summary:
This PR brings the React task run details page in ui-v2 closer to the legacy Vue page. It adds a copy button to the Task Inputs JSON, sets the browser tab title and a state-specific favicon, fixes the breadcrumb so it links to the Task Runs tab, and changes the details sidebar to always render each field, showing "None" when it is empty. The changes are small, reuse existing building blocks (`usePageTitle`, the `copy` prop on `JsonInput`, and the `/runs` route's `tab` search param), and the visible parity improvements look right.

The main problems are in the new favicon hook and in the tests. The description claims 10 unit tests for `useStateFavicon`, but no test file exists in the diff or the tree. The hook also sets the favicon to `/cancelling.svg` and `/paused.svg` for those states, which do not exist, so the tab icon will 404. In the sidebar, the new truthy check renders a valid jitter factor of `0` as "None". The sidebar rewrite also has no tests for the new empty-state branches.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The jitter-factor-0 rendering bug and the favicon 404 for CANCELLING/PAUSED are behavior problems that should be fixed before merge. The claimed favicon tests are missing even though the checklist is ticked, so the test claim should be corrected or the tests added. The remaining items are small and could be follow-ups.

architecture.overview:
The task run details page is rendered by `TaskRunDetailsPage` in `ui-v2/src/components/task-runs/task-run-details-page/index.tsx`. It fetches a `TaskRun` and passes it to `TaskRunDetails`, the sidebar in `task-run-details.tsx`. The page already had a refetch interval for RUNNING and PENDING runs, and the Runs breadcrumb pointed at `/runs` with no tab. The existing `usePageTitle` hook manages `document.title`.

This PR adds three things to that flow. It wires `usePageTitle` and a new `useStateFavicon` hook into the page so the tab title and icon follow the task run state. It rewrites the sidebar so every field renders, with "None" for empty values instead of hiding the row. It also adds a copy button to the Task Inputs JSON. The favicon hook swaps `href` on the existing `favicon-16`/`favicon-32` link elements in `index.html`, choosing the dark or light variant from the color-scheme media query.
steps: Entry point: the `/runs/task-run/$id` route renders `TaskRunDetailsPage`, which loads the `TaskRun` and passes it down.
Page wiring: `TaskRunDetailsPage` now calls `usePageTitle("Task Run: <name>")` and `useStateFavicon(taskRun.state_type)`. Both run as effects keyed on the task run values.

Favicon hook: `use-state-favicon.ts` picks the dark or light `<link>` elements from `index.html`, sets their `href` to `/<state>.svg`, and resets them to the default PNGs on cleanup. States without an SVG (CANCELLING, PAUSED) still produce a path to a missing file.
Sidebar: `TaskRunDetails` renders each field unconditionally, with a ternary that falls back to "None". The one exception is Flow Run, which now keys on `flow_run_id` alone.
Navigation and inputs: the breadcrumb adds `search={{ tab: "task-runs" }}`, which the `/runs` route validates. The Task Inputs `JsonInput` gets the existing `copy` prop.

findings.title: Claimed useStateFavicon tests are missing
findings.fixPrompt: Add `ui-v2/src/hooks/use-state-favicon.test.ts` covering `useStateFavicon` in `ui-v2/src/hooks/use-state-favicon.ts`. Follow the structure of the sibling `use-page-title.test.ts`. Mock `window.matchMedia` for both dark and light schemes, create the `favicon-16`/`favicon-32` (and `-dark`) elements in the DOM, and assert their `href` after a state is passed. Also assert the reset to default icons on unmount and the no-op when the state is null/undefined. The PR description says 10 tests exist, so either add them or correct the description and checklist.

findings.title: CANCELLING and PAUSED set the favicon to a missing SVG
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/hooks/use-state-favicon.ts`, the effect at lines 49-53 builds `/${stateType.toLowerCase()}.svg` for every state. CANCELLING and PAUSED have no SVG in `ui-v2/public`, so they 404. Only set the favicon href when the state has a matching asset, or map those states explicitly to the default icon. Keep the existing cleanup that resets to default icons. Add a test for CANCELLING to lock in the behavior.

findings.title: Retry Jitter Factor of 0 renders as "None"
findings.body:
The new ternary tests truthiness instead of nullness:

::code{file="ui-v2/src/components/task-runs/task-run-details/task-run-details.tsx" lines="177-183"}

`0` is falsy, so a jitter factor of `0`, which is a meaningful setting, displays as "None". The original code used `!== null && !== undefined`, which handled this correctly, and that is the same pattern the PR uses for Duration and Estimated Run Time.

The Run Count field (`taskRun.run_count || 0`) has the same shape. It is harmless because the fallback is also 0, but it is worth making consistent.
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/task-runs/task-run-details/task-run-details.tsx` around lines 177-183, the Retry Jitter Factor value uses a truthy check (`retry_jitter_factor ? ... : "None"`), which turns a valid 0 into "None". Change it to an explicit null/undefined check, matching the Duration and Estimated Run Time fields in the same file. Add a test in `task-run-details.test.tsx` asserting that a jitter factor of 0 renders as "0".

findings.title: Sidebar fields that now always render have no test coverage
findings.body:
The PR converts about 13 fields from conditional rendering to always-rendered, with "None" fallbacks. `task-run-details.test.tsx` was not touched. Its existing tests cover only populated cases (flow run link, task run ID, start time, tags, artifacts).

Nothing verifies that a run with no start time, no cache key, or no retry jitter shows "None" in the right row. The jitter bug above would have been caught by one test. The Task Inputs copy button and the page title/favicon wiring in `task-run-details-page/index.tsx` also have no new tests.
findings.fixPrompt: Extend `ui-v2/src/components/task-runs/task-run-details/task-run-details.test.tsx` with a case for an empty taskRun: Flow Run, Start Time, Duration, Created, Last Updated, Cache Key, Cache Expiration, Dynamic Key, Retry Delay, and Retry Jitter Factor should each show 'None'. Add a case where retry_jitter_factor is 0 that expects '0'. Follow the existing test patterns in that file.

findings.title: Flow Run link can render with an empty label
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/task-runs/task-run-details/task-run-details.tsx`, the Flow Run link (around lines 45-57) now renders whenever `flow_run_id` exists, but its label is `taskRun.flow_run_name`, which can be null. Render a fallback label (for example the flow run id) when the name is missing, so the link is never blank.

findings.title: Breadcrumb tab search param is valid
findings.body: The `/runs` route in `ui-v2/src/routes/runs/index.tsx` validates `tab` with `z.enum(["flow-runs", "task-runs"]).default("flow-runs")`. Passing `search={{ tab: "task-runs" }}` to the breadcrumb therefore resolves to the task runs tab, and TanStack Router type-checks the value. This is a clean fix for the navigation parity issue.

findings.title: Favicon element IDs exist in index.html
findings.body:
The hook looks up `favicon-16`, `favicon-32`, `favicon-16-dark`, and `favicon-32-dark`. All four are present in `ui-v2/index.html` with matching `prefers-color-scheme` media queries, so the first checklist item can be ticked.

The reset paths in the hook (`/favicon-16x16.png`) differ from the `/ico/...` defaults in index.html. Both sets of files exist in `ui-v2/public`, so this works, but the default-icon source is inconsistent.

findings.title: Page title reuses the existing usePageTitle hook
findings.body: `usePageTitle` already exists and is used by `flows/flow.$id.tsx`. Calling it with `taskRun?.name ? \`Task Run: ${taskRun.name}\` : "Task Run"` gives a sensible title while loading, and the hook resets the title on unmount. No new abstraction was added.
